I will use improved seed, not the most expensive option, because I want stable emergence and yield without raising my costs too much. Since I have well irrigation, I will rely on that to protect the crop at the key stages, but I will not irrigate too many times because the field is small and I need to keep labor manageable.

For fertilizer, I will use a moderate amount of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. Cotton needs feeding, but too much nitrogen makes the plants too leafy and can create more pest pressure, so I will keep nitrogen at a controlled level and support it with phosphorus and potassium. I will use rotary tillage because it is simpler for a small plot and easier for me to manage at the start of the season. I expect to spray pesticides several times because cotton usually needs pest control, but I will not overdo it. My goal is a steady crop, manageable work, and a reliable yield rather than taking risks.
